title: Private Access partner logins: who may log in to whose tenant, and what the user does and sees
aliases: Allow Partner Login to This Tenant
Restrict Old Zscaler Client Connector Versions to Connect to this Tenant

prose.label: Letting partners in.
prose.text: {{inbound-options}} {{restrict-old-versions}} What happens to existing macOS partner tenants when the version restriction is enabled is worded two ways {{divergence:macos-unenrollment}}.

prose.label: Pop-ups.
prose.text: {{partner-pop-ups}} The pop-up list and its other suppression intervals are in [[zcc.notifications.pop-ups]].

prose.label: Open questions.
prose.text: How partner login relates to application federation is not stated by the partner login pages {{gap:b2b-federation-relation}}; the federation feature is [[zpa.b2b-federation]]. The app profile's partner login settings are not described in these pages {{gap:app-profile-partner-settings}}.

what-a-partner-is.statement: A partner is a separate entity or company that owns a Private Access tenant. An organization can give partner organizations access to its tenant and allow its users to access a partner organization's tenant; the partner must configure the same settings for its own tenant for users of both to reach each other's tenants. Partner login is configured under Private Access > B2B Exchange > Partner Login.

quotes: A partner is a separate entity or company that owns a Private Access tenant.
You can give partner organizations access to your organization's tenant. You can also allow your users to access a partner organization's tenant.
A partner organization must have these same settings configured for their own tenant as well to ensure users from your organization and their organization can access each other's tenants.
From the navigation menu, go to Private Access > B2B Exchange > Partner Login.

inbound-options.statement: Allow Partner Login to This Tenant offers the choices No Access, Specific Tenants and All Tenants. No Access disallows access to the tenant to any partner organization. Specific Tenants takes a Primary Tenant Domain, a fully qualified domain name for the partner tenant, and if no cloud name is entered a user on the partner domain on any cloud name can access the tenant; Specific Tenants applies only to Client Connector 4.7 and later for Windows and 5.0 and later for macOS. All Tenants gives access to all partner organizations.

quotes: No Access: Select this option to disallow access to your tenant to any partner organizations.
Primary Tenant Domain: Enter a fully qualified domain name (FQDN) for the partner tenant.
If no cloudname is entered, a user on the partner domain on any cloudname can access your tenant.
The Specific Tenants option applies only to Zscaler Client Connector 4.7 and later for Windows and Zscaler Client Connector version 5.0 and later for macOS.
All Tenants: Select this option to give access to your tenant to all partner organizations.

restrict-old-versions.statement: Under Specific Tenants, Restrict Old Zscaler Client Connector Versions to Connect to this Tenant, when enabled, allows only partner tenant devices using Client Connector 4.7 and later for Windows and 5.0 and later for macOS to log in to the tenant.

quotes: Specific Tenants: Select this option to allow access to your tenant by specific tenants:

Restrict Old Zscaler Client Connector Versions to Connect to this Tenant: Enable to allow only partner tenant devices using Zscaler Client Connector version 4.7 and later for Windows and Zscaler Client Connector version 5.0 and later for macOS to log in to this tenant.

outbound-login.statement: Allow Users of This Tenant to Log in to Other Tenants lets the organization's users access a partner's tenant and is disabled by default. On Client Connector 4.6 and later for Windows or 5.0 and later for macOS, access to a partner's tenant can be configured on the app profile, and partner login settings enabled on the app profile override these settings.

quotes: Enable Allow Users of This Tenant to Log in to Other Tenants to let your users access a partner's tenant. By default, this setting is disabled.
If you use Zscaler Client Connector version 4.6 and later for Windows or Zscaler Client Connector version 5.0 and later for macOS, you can configure access to a partner's tenant on the app profile.
Partner login settings that are enabled on the app profile override these settings.

user-adds-tenant.statement: A user can add a partner tenant to the app to access the partner's internal resources without logging out of and back in to Client Connector, once the organization and the partner organization have enabled Private Access partner logins, which can be enabled even when only Internet & SaaS is used. On Windows, if the organization does not use Private Access, the Private Access window shows only the Add Partner Tenant link and information about the partner tenant. Based on the partner tenant settings, the user is prompted to complete one of the steps the page lists, one of which is selecting the partner tenant and clicking Connect, and the identity provider page for the partner organization then appears.

quotes: You can add a partner tenant to the app so that you can access the partner's internal resources without needing to log out of and back in to Zscaler Client Connector.
Before you can add a partner tenant, your organization and the partner organization must enable Private Access partner logins.
You can enable Private Access partner logins even if you do not use Private Access and use only Internet & SaaS.

evidence.after: To add a partner tenant using the Windows version
quotes: If your organization does not use Private Access, the Private Access window displays only the Add Partner Tenant link and information about the partner tenant.
Based on your organization's partner tenant settings, you are prompted to complete one of the following steps:
Select the partner tenant to access and click Connect.
The identity provider page for the partner organization appears.

one-tenant-at-a-time.statement: In the Windows steps of the Classic UI page, after the user logs in to the partner organization Client Connector automatically turns off Private Access access to the user's own organization, and clicking Turn On for the main tenant enables it and turns off access to the partner organization. The partner tenant remains in the window, and Turn On for it enables Private Access access to the partner organization.

evidence.after: To add a partner tenant using the Windows version
quotes: After logging in to the partner organization, Zscaler Client Connector automatically turns off Private Access access to your organization.
You can click Turn On for the main tenant to enable it and automatically turn off access to the partner organization.
After you have added the partner tenant, the partner tenant remains on this window, and you can click Turn On for the partner tenant to enable Private Access access to the partner organization.

partner-pop-ups.statement: Client Connector shows Partner Private Access is Connected and Partner Private Access is Disconnected as Service Status pop-ups for Private Access, and duplicates of each that display within a 1-minute interval are suppressed. The pop-up list applies to Client Connector 4.4 and later for Windows and 4.3 and later for macOS.

quotes: | Private Access | Service Status | Partner Private Access is Connected. | None required. | Duplicate messages that display within a 1-minute interval are suppressed. |
| Private Access | Service Status | Partner Private Access is Disconnected. | None required. | Duplicate messages that display within a 1-minute interval are suppressed. |
This list applies only to Zscaler Client Connector version 4.4 and later for Windows and for Zscaler Client Connector version 4.3 and later for macOS.

macos-unenrollment.summary: One option on the partner login page says only partner devices on Client Connector 5.0 and later for macOS may log in, and in the next sentence says enabling it unenrolls existing partner tenants using Client Connector for macOS without a version bound.

quotes: Restrict Old Zscaler Client Connector Versions to Connect to this Tenant: Enable to allow only partner tenant devices using Zscaler Client Connector version 4.7 and later for Windows and Zscaler Client Connector version 5.0 and later for macOS to log in to this tenant.

positions.says: With the option enabled, partner devices on 4.7 and later for Windows and 5.0 and later for macOS can log in.

quotes: If you enable this option, any existing partner tenants using Zscaler Client Connector for macOS or version 4.6 and earlier for Windows are unenrolled.

positions.says: With the option enabled, existing partner tenants using Client Connector for macOS (no version given) or 4.6 and earlier for Windows are unenrolled.

macos-unenrollment.impact: Read literally, the second sentence unenrolls every macOS partner tenant, including those on 5.0 and later that the first sentence allows; the page does not say which governs.

b2b-federation-relation.title: How partner login relates to B2B application federation
b2b-federation-relation.detail: The partner login pages place the setting under Private Access > B2B Exchange but do not say whether it uses or depends on application federation.

app-profile-partner-settings.title: The app profile's partner login settings
app-profile-partner-settings.detail: What the app profile's partner login settings are, and what they contain, is not described in the partner login pages.
